TEXT 1
Government defends axing century-old banyans on safety grounds
[1] Four trees collapsed in Hong Kong on Monday morning following a night of heavy
rain. This comes after the government’s controversial decision to cut down four
century-old Chinese banyans after several similar trees fell from stone walls during recent
storms.
[2] The report of the fallen trees comes days after experts expressed anger over the
Highways Department’s controversial felling of four century-old banyan trees in Sai
Ying Pun, without consulting a panel advising the government on tree management.
[3] The government cited ‘unforeseen’ circumstances and considerations of public
safety, after a giant banyan tree growing out of a masonry wall in Sai Ying Pun collapsed
on 22 July. A neighbouring tree was cut down immediately as cracks were found in the
wall behind it.
[4] The Head of the Developments Bureau’s Tree Management Office said the trees in
Sai Ying Pun were rooted in old stone masonry walls on a slope of almost 80 degrees.

TEXT 2
A Tree Worthy of Worship: Hong Kong’s Banyans
[1] Mr Lam was a teenager when he installed a shrine to the local earth god under a
banyan tree in Tai Hang. “That was over 70 years ago,” he says. After World War II, he
received permission from the government to transform the shrine into a temple.
[2] It is no coincidence that Lam’s temple started with a banyan tree. These behemoths
are ubiquitous in Hong Kong, growing in parks, street planters and even between the
cracks of stone walls. Their imposing presence defines the cityscape. “If Hong Kong was
abandoned it would be taken over by banyans in a few hundred years,” says Jim
Chi-yung, chair of the University of Hong Kong’s Department of Geography, who is
popularly known as the Tree Professor for his arboreal enthusiasm.
[3] Banyan trees are immediately recognisable for their spindly aerial roots, which cast
outwards in search of water and nutrition. When a root finds a suitable source, either in
the soil or another tree, it becomes a thick, woody trunk. This is what allows the banyan
to grow in varied conditions, which is why they are the most prominent forms of
greenery in the hilliest and most densely packed parts of Hong Kong. Jim has counted
more than 1,100 trees growing from the sheer surfaces of masonry walls on Hong Kong
Island. “They can become 20 metres tall, as big as trees growing out of the ground,
except they are growing out from the wall,” he says.

[4] When I first met Jim, in 2009, he took me to Forbes Street in Kennedy Town, where
22 banyans grow out of the surface of a 12-metre-high stone wall, which was built using
a traditional Hakka technique that does not require mortar between stone joints. Seeds
carried by the wind or dropped by birds find their way into the cracks. As the tree grows,
its roots plunge dozens of metres into the soil behind the wall.
[5] Jim loves the way the banyans form a lush green canopy across Forbes Street. He sits
on a number of government committees, and he told me he once proposed
pedestrianising the street to make it a destination for al fresco dining, a place where
people could sit and relax under the shade of the banyans. The government’s reception
was frosty.
[6] “See what’s happening here?” he asks, touching a root that had been concreted over
to stop it from growing. “The people who do this, they don’t understand trees. They’re
defacing heritage. Imagine doing this to an ancient monument.”
[7] Last summer, after days of heavy rain, a wall tree collapsed onto Bonham Road,
which led the Highways Department to surreptitiously chop down four healthy banyans
nearby. Their sudden removal was defended by the government as a precautionary
measure, but experts like Jim said it was an unnecessary overreaction. It sparked outrage
from local residents, who tied balloons and messages of support to the trees’ roots,
which still clung to the wall that had supported them for 100 years.

[8] Respect for banyans runs deep in southern Chinese culture. Banyan trees are
considered to have excellent feng shui, symbolising longevity, fecundity and
perseverance. They are also believed to be home to earth gods, the indigenous deities
that protect each village, and shrines are often built at their base. In many cases, people
worship the trees themselves, not just the earth gods. That is the case in Lam Tsuen,
where a pair of banyans known as the Wishing Trees have become a tourist attraction.
Visitors write their wish on a piece of yellow paper, tie it to an orange and toss it onto
one of the trees’ branches. After the weight of all the wishes caused a branch to collapse
in 2005, worshippers were instructed to tie their wishes to a plastic tree instead.
[9] Anthropologist P.Y.L. Ng notes that banyan trees were worshipped because they
were often the only surviving trees in a landscape that had been steadily deforested over
hundreds of years. “Its wood is gnarled and so cannot be used as timber. It will not flame
and so cannot be used for firewood. Its very lack of useful properties ensures its
invincibility and survival,” he wrote in a 1983 study of the New Territories.
[10] The 17th century playwright Li Yu saw the banyan tree as a symbol of love.
“Anytime a smaller tree grows before a banyan tree, this banyan will sooner or later lean
its body towards the smaller tree. After a time, it wraps its branches around the smaller
tree’s body, and the smaller tree gradually falls into the banyan’s embrace. The two trees
become one, so that even if you cut them with an axe you would not be able to separate
them.”

[11] Modern Hong Kong has found ways to accommodate banyan trees. To Yuen Street
near City University forks around a particularly large banyan, an accommodation also
made on Dragon Road near Victoria Park. Nearly two-thirds of the 481 trees on the
government’s Register of Old and Valuable Trees are banyans. According to the
government, there are 29,000 banyans under maintenance in city parks and streets,
though many more exist undocumented in the wild. A total of 3,491 new banyans have
been planted in the city since 2011.
[12] And while the future of many old and prominent banyans is contentious you can
count on banyans to find a way to survive even in the most difficult conditions. New
sprouts are already growing from the stumps of the severed banyan trees on Bonham
Road. There is a reason they are worshipped, after all.

Paragraph 3（第三段）
Description（描寫）
Banyan trees are immediately recognisable for their spindly aerial roots, which
cast outwards in search of water and nutrition.
榕樹最容易辨認的特徵，是它們細長的氣根；這些氣根會向外伸展，尋找水
分與養分。
Explanation（解釋）
When a root finds a suitable source, either in the soil or another tree, it becomes
a thick, woody trunk.
當一條根找到合適的來源，不論是在土壤中還是在另一棵樹上，它便會變成
粗壯而木質化的樹幹。
Explanation（解釋）
This is what allows the banyan to grow in varied conditions, which is why they
are the most prominent forms of greenery in the hilliest and most densely
packed parts of Hong Kong.
這正是榕樹能在不同環境中生長的原因，也解釋了為甚麼它們會成為香港
最陡峭、最擠迫地區中最顯眼的綠化植物。

Respect for banyans runs deep in southern Chinese culture.

Paragraph 2 說榕樹在香港無處不在，塑造城市景觀。
Paragraph 3 解釋榕樹的氣根與生長適應力。
Paragraph 4 用 Forbes Street 的石牆榕樹作具體例子。
Paragraph 5 展示 Jim Chi-yung 對榕樹街景的欣賞，以及政府對保育構想反應
Paragraph 6 顯示 Jim 對把根部封上石屎的做法非常不滿。
Paragraph 7 回到 Bonham Road／Sai Ying Pun 一帶砍樹事件，指出居民憤怒。
Paragraph 8 講榕樹在華南文化中的風水、長壽、多產、土地神、許願樹意義
Paragraph 9 用 P. Y. L. Ng 的研究解釋榕樹因「沒有實用木材價值」而存活。
Paragraph 10 用 Li Yu 的文字說榕樹象徵愛。
Paragraph 11 說現代香港也有方法容納榕樹，例如道路繞過榕樹、政府名冊、
Paragraph 12 用被砍榕樹樁上重新長芽作結，突出榕樹的頑強生命力。

The trees could have collapsed and pulled the wall with them.
即樹木可能倒下，倒下時把牆一起拉倒。
所以 them 指 trees。

是被拉的對象，不是 them。

前文有 “the department”，但 department 不會 collapse，也不會把牆一起拉下。
代詞指代要看語義動作是否合理。
能 collapse 的是 trees，不是 department

題目問甚麼
這是 inference 題。
不能只把句子翻譯成「榕樹會佔領香港」。要問 Jim 為何用這種誇張畫面。
原文定位
Paragraph 2 說榕樹在香港很普遍：
“growing in parks, street planters and even between the cracks of stone walls.”
“They define the cityscape.”
接著 Jim 說：
“If Hong Kong was abandoned it would be taken over by banyans in a few hundred
years.”
答案與推理
Jim 的說法帶有假設和誇張，但意思很清楚：
榕樹很會生長
不需要理想泥土也能活
石牆裂縫、街道、山坡都能成為生長點
只要人類停止管理城市，榕樹會慢慢擴張
這句也呼應 paragraph 3 的生物解釋：banyan roots search for water and
nutrition，能在 varied conditions 中生長。

這題考甚麼？
這題表面是 summary completion MC，
但真正考的是 paraphrase mapping，
即「原文表達」如何轉成「摘要中的另一種說法」。
它考你三種能力：
第一，能不能把 canopy 理解成有遮蓋功能的東西。
第二，能不能把 pedestrianising the street 理解成把街道改為行人使用、減少
或排除車輛。
第三，能不能把 frosty reception 理解成冷淡、不支持、負面的反應。
這題最容易錯的地方是：三個空格的正確答案都不是直接照抄原文。
可是錯項中有一些字曾在原文出現，特別是 destination。這種題非常典型：正
確答案往往是概念改寫；錯答案常常借用原文附近的字，
讓學生覺得「我見過這個字，所以好像對」。
所以，這題不能用「有沒有在原文出現」來判斷。要用以下三角比對：
原文意思 ↔ 題目空格語法 ↔ 選項概念

原文定位
Paragraph 10 引 Li Yu：
“Anytime a smaller tree grows before a banyan tree, this banyan will sooner or later lean
its body towards the smaller tree.”
“it wraps its branches around the smaller tree’s body”

榕樹向小樹傾斜

兩棵樹合為一體
即使用斧頭也分不開
最完整答案是：
The banyan leans towards a smaller tree and wraps its branches
around it until the two become one.

Paragraph 10 引 Li Yu：
“Anytime a smaller tree grows before a banyan tree, this banyan will sooner or later lean

“it wraps its branches around the smaller tree’s body”
“The two trees become one…”

可答以下任一重點：
榕樹向小樹傾斜
榕樹用枝條環抱小樹
小樹落入榕樹懷抱
兩棵樹合為一體
即使用斧頭也分不開
最完整答案是：
The banyan leans towards a smaller tree and wraps its branches
around it until the two become one.

它其實考 voice matching，即「哪一句話最像哪個人物或機構會說」。
所以學生不能只看某個字有沒有出現。要看四件事：

第二，這個人物對榕樹的態度是甚麼。
第三，這句 comment 的語氣是否符合那個人物。
第四，這句 comment 是否抓住該段的核心意思。
例如 B 說 “There are too many trees growing out of walls.”
這句有 “trees growing out of walls”，很容易令人想到 Jim Chi-yung，
因為 Jim 確實 counted more than 1,100 trees growing from masonry walls。
可是 Jim 的態度不是嫌牆樹太多。他欣賞榕樹，也批評破壞榕樹根部的人。所
以 B 是典型的 keyword trap：有相同內容詞，但態度錯。

這句不是要表達人物真的討厭榕樹。

所以 F 的 “useless” 要理解為「沒有實用木材價值」，

為何 Jim 不能配 B
B 是這題最大陷阱：
B. There are too many trees growing out of walls.
學生會被這句吸引，因為 paragraph 3 說：
“Jim has counted more than 1,100 trees growing from the sheer surfaces of masonry
walls on Hong Kong Island.”
所以有些學生會想：
Jim 提到很多牆上樹，B 也說很多牆上樹，所以 Jim = B。
這樣配會錯，因為 B 的語氣是抱怨：
“There are too many...”
= 太多了，帶負面評價
Jim 的語氣完全不同。他不是抱怨牆樹太多。
他欣賞它們，保護它們，批評破壞它們的人。
他甚至提議把 Forbes Street pedestrianised，讓人坐在榕樹蔭下享受街道。
所以 B 抓住了 “trees growing out of walls” 這個表面關鍵字，
卻把 Jim 的態度改錯。
這是典型的 same-keyword, wrong-attitude trap。

全題總結
而是以下幾種精準閱讀能力：
1. 事件分流
Text 1 Q1 很典型：四棵樹倒塌與四棵百年榕樹被砍是兩件不同事件。
2. 程序與原因辨認
Q2 要知道爭議點不是單純砍樹，而是砍百年樹且沒有諮詢顧問小組。
3. T/F/NG 的精準判斷
Q5 和 Q18 都要求分清：
有支持 = T
有相反 = F
沒有資料 = NG
4. 代詞指代
Q4、Q14 都要把代詞放回句子，看哪個名詞語義合理。
5. 詞義與段落範圍控制
Q10 的 imposing 很容易被 paragraph 3 的 prominent 干擾。題目限定
paragraph 2，就不能跨段。
6. summary correction 的詞性與語義控制
Q11 考 roots / branches、source / protection、thick / thin、varied / few。每個
都是同段資訊錯配。
7. 文化意義與生物特徵分開
Text 2 同時談 worship、feng shui、aerial roots、stone walls、heritage、
government policy。答題時要按題目定位，不要把另一段的意思搬來。
8. 語氣判斷
Q15、Q16、Q23 都要看態度詞：frosty、defacing heritage、unnecessary
overreaction、precautionary measure。
9. 結尾推論
Q22 的重點在最後幾句：survive、difficult conditions、new sprouts、stumps。
答案應落在 resilience / perseverance。
